summary: Markets are consolidating near all-time highs after the S&P 500 broke above 7,800 for the first time this week, though Friday's session saw modest pullbacks as consumer sentiment data disappointed. The University of Michigan Index plunged to 51.0 in August from 55.2 in July, with inflation expectations ticking higher to 4.3% amid lingering concerns about the Iran conflict's impact on energy prices. Despite the softer sentiment reading, equity markets have absorbed recent inflation data well, with July CPI showing a benign 0.1% monthly increase and 3.4% year-over-year rise, keeping Fed rate-hike fears at bay after the July FOMC meeting saw three dissents pushing for tightening. Crypto markets are showing renewed institutional appetite, with Bitcoin ETFs posting their strongest weekly inflows since April at over $853 million as BTC reclaimed the $65,000 level. BlackRock's IBIT continues to dominate flows, signaling traditional finance's growing comfort with digital assets even as Bitcoin remains down 27% year-to-date and nearly 49% below its October 2025 all-time high above $126,000.

signals.title: Consumer Sentiment Collapses Despite Recent Improvement
signals.desc: University of Michigan Index fell 8% to 51.0 in August, ending two months of gains as business conditions expectations sank 11-17%, pointing to renewed caution that could weigh on consumer spending.

signals.title: S&P 500 Breaks 7,800 for First Time on Broad Sector Strength
signals.desc: The benchmark index hit an all-time intraday high above 7,800 and closed at a record 7,798.99 on Thursday, led by energy's 6% weekly surge and outperformance in healthcare and financials.

signals.title: July CPI Shows Muted Inflation, Keeps Fed on Hold
signals.desc: July CPI rose just 0.1% month-over-month and 3.4% year-over-year, easing immediate rate-hike pressure despite three FOMC dissents in July, supporting the view that the Fed will pause in September.

signals.title: Bitcoin ETF Inflows Hit $850M as Institutional Demand Surges
signals.desc: US Bitcoin ETFs posted their strongest weekly inflows since April at over $850 million, with Bitcoin breaking decisively above $65,000 as BlackRock's IBIT captures the lion's share of institutional capital.

signals.title: Retail Sales and Sentiment Point to Slowing Economic Engine
signals.desc: Declines in consumer sentiment and retail sales have overshadowed Fed pause optimism, raising concerns about Corporate America's growth prospects even as the S&P 500 notched a third straight weekly gain.

verdict: Markets are digesting record highs against deteriorating consumer confidence, with the Fed pause narrative intact but growth concerns emerging as a new risk factor for the September session.
